quizName: DMV Practice Test #8 25 Questions • Passing Score 20

questions.question: What is the best way to stop quickly?

options.text: Use the front brake only.
Use the rear brake first.
Throttle down and use the front brake.
Use both brakes at the same time.

questions.correctAnswerText: Use both brakes at the same time.
questions.explanation: To stop quickly, press both brakes at the same time. Apply firm pressure and stay calm if the brakes lock.

questions.question: Which type of sign is yellow with black lettering or symbols?

options.text: Warning
Service
Regulatory
Speed limit

questions.correctAnswerText: Warning
questions.explanation: Warning signs are yellow with black lettering or symbols. They tell drivers about dangerous road conditions ahead.

questions.question: What do studies show about motorcycles with headlights on during the day?

options.text: They are not as easy to see as other vehicles.
Other drivers see them better than when the headlights are off.
Other drivers are often confused.
They are less safe than when the headlights are off.

questions.correctAnswerText: Other drivers see them better than when the headlights are off.
questions.explanation: Keep your headlight on whenever you ride. During the day, a motorcycle with the headlight on is twice as likely to be noticed by other drivers.

questions.question: A rectangular sign may be a:

options.text: School crossing sign.
Railroad crossing sign.
Stop sign.
Speed limit sign.

questions.correctAnswerText: Speed limit sign.
questions.explanation: Regulatory signs like speed limit signs are rectangular and white with black lettering. You must follow the rules shown on these signs.

questions.question: Curved mirrors make cars look:

options.text: Larger.
Farther away.
Faster.
Narrower.

questions.correctAnswerText: Farther away.
questions.explanation: Curved mirrors show a wider view of the road than flat mirrors. However, they make objects appear farther away than they really are.

questions.question: If hazards are on your left, where should you ride?

options.text: In the left portion of the lane.
In the right portion of the lane.
In any portion of the lane.
On the shoulder.

questions.correctAnswerText: In the right portion of the lane.
questions.explanation: When hazards are on your left, ride in the right portion of the lane. Adjust your position as road and traffic conditions change.

questions.question: Where should you ride to be seen in the rearview mirror of the car ahead?

options.text: In the center portion of the lane.
In the left portion of the lane.
In the right portion of the lane.
In a weaving pattern.

questions.correctAnswerText: In the center portion of the lane.
questions.explanation: Ride in the center of your lane behind a car. This puts you in the driver's rearview mirror. Most drivers check their rearview mirror more often than their side mirrors.

questions.question: How do you maintain control of your motorcycle while turning?

options.text: Speed up before entering the turn.
Keep the motorcycle from leaning.
Look through the turn to plan the best path.
Come to a complete stop before entering the turn.

questions.correctAnswerText: Look through the turn to plan the best path.
questions.explanation: To stay in control through a turn, look through the turn by turning only your head. Slow down before the turn and lean your motorcycle in the right direction.

questions.question: When carrying a passenger or cargo, what happens?

options.text: It takes less time to speed up, but more time to stop.
It takes more time to speed up and stop.
It takes more time to speed up, but less time to stop.
It takes less time to speed up and stop.

questions.correctAnswerText: It takes more time to speed up and stop.
questions.explanation: Extra weight from a passenger or cargo makes your motorcycle take longer to speed up and stop.

questions.question: Why are signals important on a motorcycle?

options.text: They serve little purpose since motorcycles are smaller than most vehicles.
They tell other drivers what you plan to do.
You should not use them if no vehicles are nearby.
They are more complicated than car signals.

questions.correctAnswerText: They tell other drivers what you plan to do.
questions.explanation: As a motorcycle rider, you are more vulnerable. Always use turn signals to tell others what you plan to do. Use them whenever you change lanes or turn, even if you think no one is nearby.

questions.question: Is it legal to ride between two vehicles moving in the same direction?

options.text: No, it is illegal.
Yes, if traffic is heavy.
Yes, during the day to prevent traffic jams.
Yes, if the motorcyclist is comfortable with it.

questions.correctAnswerText: No, it is illegal.
questions.explanation: In Oregon, motorcycles and mopeds cannot ride between two moving vehicles on a multilane highway or one-way street.

questions.question: When should you increase your following distance?

options.text: When the pavement is dry.
When the pavement is wet.
When you can see through the vehicle ahead.
When the sun is out.

questions.correctAnswerText: When the pavement is wet.
questions.explanation: You need more space to stop on wet pavement. Increase your following distance if the road is slippery, if you cannot see around the vehicle ahead, or if traffic is heavy and another driver might cut in front of you.

questions.question: In group riding, what does this hand signal mean?

options.text: Speed up.
Danger ahead.
Stop.
Merge.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stop.
questions.explanation: Hand signals help riders communicate in groups. When the lead rider extends their left arm straight down with their palm facing back, all riders should stop.

questions.question: What is true about the front brake?

options.text: Use it only when you need to stop quickly.
Use it only on slippery roads.
It is less effective than the rear brake.
It is safe to use if you use it properly.

questions.correctAnswerText: It is safe to use if you use it properly.
questions.explanation: Use both brakes every time you slow down or stop. The front brake is more powerful than the rear brake and is safe to use when you use it correctly.

questions.question: Where do most conflicts happen between motorcyclists and other drivers?

options.text: At intersections
On highways
On rural roads
In parking lots

questions.correctAnswerText: At intersections
questions.explanation: Intersections are where most conflicts happen between motorcyclists and other drivers. Ride with extra caution when you approach and go through intersections.

questions.question: What is a danger of riding directly alongside another vehicle?

options.text: You may be in the driver's blind spot.
It is safer than riding behind the vehicle.
It is safe because you have limited escape routes.
You should only do it during the day.

questions.correctAnswerText: You may be in the driver's blind spot.
questions.explanation: Do not ride directly alongside another vehicle because the driver may not see you in their blind spot and could move into your lane without warning. Riding alongside also blocks your escape route if danger appears.

questions.question: Which of these gives a rider the best protection?

options.text: Goggles
A face shield
A windshield
Eyeglasses

questions.correctAnswerText: A face shield
questions.explanation: A plastic, shatter-resistant face shield protects your entire face in a crash. Goggles protect only your eyes. A windshield or eyeglasses do not provide enough protection.

questions.question: What should you do when riding with a passenger because of the added weight?

options.text: Ride slower than usual.
Keep a shorter following distance than when riding alone.
Ride faster than usual.
Brake a little later than when riding alone.

questions.correctAnswerText: Ride slower than usual.
questions.explanation: A passenger adds weight, so your motorcycle takes longer to speed up, slow down, and turn. Reduce your speed, start braking earlier, increase your following distance, and look for larger gaps when crossing, entering, or merging with traffic.

questions.question: When should a motorcyclist shift gears?

options.text: During a turn.
Before a turn.
By changing power suddenly in a turn.
While riding the brake through a turn.

questions.correctAnswerText: Before a turn.
questions.explanation: Shift gears before you enter a turn.

questions.question: What should you do if you cannot avoid a slippery road?

options.text: Lean into the slippery section to stay balanced.
Keep your speed the same to improve traction.
Do not worry about the road conditions.
Keep your motorcycle upright and go as slowly as needed.

questions.correctAnswerText: Keep your motorcycle upright and go as slowly as needed.
questions.explanation: Avoid slippery roads completely if you can. If you cannot avoid one, keep your motorcycle upright and go as slowly as possible.

questions.question: Lane sharing is:

options.text: Usually not allowed.
Encouraged in heavy traffic areas.
Safe because motorcycles don't need a full lane.
Allowed if you've had your license for more than three years.

questions.correctAnswerText: Usually not allowed.
questions.explanation: Motorcycles need a full lane width to operate safely, just like cars. Lane sharing is usually not allowed. Position your motorcycle in the lane to discourage other vehicles from trying to share it.

questions.question: A properly fitted motorcycle:

options.text: Lets the rider touch the ground with their feet while sitting.
Has a seat level with the rider's waist.
Has a seat 10 inches above the rider's waist.
Has a seat 10 inches below the rider's waist.

questions.correctAnswerText: Lets the rider touch the ground with their feet while sitting.
questions.explanation: A properly fitted motorcycle allows your feet to reach the ground while you sit on it. When riding, keep your feet firmly on the footrests.

questions.question: Where is the gearshift lever?

options.text: In front of the left footrest
In front of the right footrest
On the left handgrip
On the right handgrip

questions.correctAnswerText: In front of the left footrest
questions.explanation: The gearshift lever is in front of the left footrest. You operate it with your left foot.

questions.question: When approaching an intersection, you should:

options.text: Assume other drivers see you, especially if they make eye contact.
Never assume other drivers see you.
Stay focused on moving through the intersection.
Speed up to make others notice you.

questions.correctAnswerText: Never assume other drivers see you.
questions.explanation: Never assume that other drivers see you, even if they look at you. Drivers often look directly at motorcyclists but still don't notice them. Always slow down when approaching an intersection.

questions.question: A motorcyclist is well protected if they wear:

options.text: A jacket that leaves the arms exposed.
Boots with tall heels.
Leather gloves.
Shoes that stop below the ankle.

questions.correctAnswerText: Leather gloves.
questions.explanation: For protection while riding, wear a jacket and pants that fully cover your arms and legs. Boots or shoes should be tall and sturdy to cover and support your ankles. Use footwear with low heels that won't catch on foot pegs or rough surfaces. Leather gloves or gloves made of another durable material protect your hands in a crash and improve your grip on the controls.
